News.title: Moscow explosion: Three dead and 21 injured after bomb detonates at busy restaurant
News.content:
Moscow explosion: Three dead and 21 injured after bomb detonates at busy restaurant

Three people have been killed as more fight for their live in hospital after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russia

View 3 Images The bomber, a security guard and a visitor to the restaurant are said to have died (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

An explosion at a restaurant in ‌central ⁠Moscow has killed at least three people, according to Russian state media.

‌



At least 21 people were injured in the explosion with some left fighting for their lives as investigators, forensic experts and emergency services continue working at the scene. A homemade explosive device was detonated at the Italian eatery in Kudrinskaya Square.

‌



The bomber, as well as a security guard and a diner, died in the blast at the trendy Balzi Rossi. The National Anti-Terrorist Committee said a woman carrying explosives attempted to enter the restaurant but was stopped. The device then went off, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor.

‌



View 3 Images Police take security measures at the scene in Moscow (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The blast happened at around 8pm local time (5pm UK). The attack is still being investigated, the Moscow Investigative Committee told the RIA news agency, who released a video showing heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene. Roads nearby have been closed off to members of the public.

Witnesses said they saw people leaving covered in blood following the explosion. Authorities have not named those killed or injured and have yet say who they thought might have been responsible.

‌



Those injured in the attack had received wounds of varying seriousness, according to police.

View 3 Images The restaurant is located in one of the city's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The exclusive restaurant's website stated that it was closed on Saturday for private event on its outdoor terrace.

Article continues below

Balzi Rossi is located at the base of the Kudrinskaya Square Building, one of Moscow’s Stalinist skyscrapers, which were built in the 1950s.

“We’re all fine, and our restaurant and kitchen are in perfect condition; there was just a minor issue at the restaurant entrance,” Balzi Rossi chef Carmine Alfieri said on Instagram without elaborating further.

Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride.

News.title: Several injured as 'overcrowded' North London festival halted and police called
News.content:
Several injured as 'overcrowded' North London festival halted and police called

The Ghana Party in the Park in Barnet was 'temporarily paused', according to organisers.

View Image Police were called to the scene (file photo) (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

A cultural festival in London was halted this evening (Saturday) after several people were injured. The Ghana Party in the Park in Barnet was 'temporarily paused', according to organisers.

‌



Police said that they attended the site of the event at Copthall Playing Fields due to an 'overcrowding issue'. Several people had been injured, police added, but none of the injuries are life-threatening in nature.

‌



Met Police in Barnet said: "Officers are at Copthall Playing Fields where Ghana Party in the Park has been cancelled after an overcrowding issue at the entrance saw several people sustain non-life threatening injuries. Speculation about a stabbing is inaccurate. Please help us by avoiding the area."

‌



Organisers of the event posted on social media: "Due to a major incident at the festival site, the event has been temporarily paused. Please do not travel to or come to the festival site until further notice.

"The emergency services and relevant authorities are currently managing the situation. We kindly ask everyone to stay away from the area to allow them to carry out their work safely.

Article continues below

"We will provide further updates as soon as more information becomes available. Thank you for your patience, understanding, and cooperation."

News.title: Naples earthquake recap: Italy struck by 4.7 magnitude quake as rocks crush cars
News.content:
The quake has caused a massive landslide in Pozzuoli

Residents in Naples have been left terrified after a powerful earthquake caused damage to the Italian city - it registered at 4.7 magnitude

A powerful earthquake struck southern Italy, causing damage in the city of Naples.

The 4.7 magnitude quake has left neighbourhoods without power, and residents are taking to the streets in fear. It occurred just before 8pm (local time).

According to data released by the INGV (National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology), the magnitude was 4.7. Power outages have been reported from Pizzofalcone to Fuorigrotta, and there has been a massive landslide in Pozzuoli.

Images show buildings have crumbled, with debris crushing cars.

Thank you for following our live blog. It has now ended.

News.title: Golden retriever defies vets to survive FIVE surgeries after he's bitten by a snake
News.content:
Golden retriever defies vets to survive FIVE surgeries after he's bitten by a snake

Beloved puppy Kobi suddenly fell ill after going out for walk with his owner Roma Morgan, who had no idea her pet had been bitten by an adder in Aberystwyth, west Wales

View 4 Images Kobi was bitten by an adder in Aberystwyth, Wales (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

A fearless Golden retriever shook off five surgeries to defy vets after being bitten by an adder.

‌



Kobi had been walking through long grass when he suddenly became "very lethargic". His owner Roma Morgan rushed the seven-month-old pup to her local vets, where he had blood tests and painkillers but continued to fall ill and and cried when touched.

‌



It was only when they shaved Kobi's swollen neck that a traumatic puncture wound was discovered - and her pet was then taken to another vet for a second opinion and given anti-venom. But over the next 10 months, he underwent five separate operations and 90 wound dressing changes with treatment costing more than £8,000.

‌



Roma, of Penparcau, near Aberystwth, west Wales, says she and husband Steve are "forever grateful" to the vets who "gave him the care he needed" She is now warning others of the risks of adder bites to their dogs but says seeing Kobi finally recovered brought her so much joy.

Millions of UK dog owners issued crucial garden advice by Monty Don READ MORE :

View 4 Images Owner Roma Morgan rushed her dog to the vet where he had blood tests and painkillers (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

She said: "It was best feeling. Seeing him running and swimming makes it all worthwhile. He's our little hero." Friends began a fundraising page to help Roma and Steve pay for Kobi's treatement in June last year.

‌



The page read: "Kobi, just a curious baby golden retriever, whilst playing in the river was bitten by an adder. He didn't make a fuss, and nobody witnessed it.

"He became very poorly, very quickly, and eventually it was realised that he'd been bitten by a venomous snake. It was already at advanced stages in his system by this time.

"A long, heartbreaking fight to save Kobi began from that moment. Roma and her husband Steve sourced anti venom and drove away to collect it.

‌



View 4 Images Kobi needed months to recover from his injuries (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

"The veterinarians began the slow process of fixing their boy, bearing in mind that he would not suffer more than he needed to. It was feared that his organs would fail, but he pulled through with intensive care.

"His skin perished and he has bravely endured multiple surgeries which will continue until all the fluid build ups are cleared and his skin is healed. He is a champion, he survived on love."

‌



Adders are the only venomous snake native to the UK and are protected by the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

View 4 Images His owner is now warning dog owners about the dangers of adders (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

Warning about stomach complaint that can be fatal

Last month, a vet warned dog owners to bring their pets into their local practice immediately if they notice one change in their body - as it could be fatal. It can sometimes be difficult to know if and when you should take your pet to the vets, and if an issue is a genuine emergency.

‌



In a TikTok video, vets at Green Pastures Vets in Weston-super-Mare, Somerset, ran through two scenarios that commonly arise in dogs, weighing in on whether each one constitutes an emergency.

One of the vets asked: "Kathleen, emergency or not, a dog shaking for no obvious reason?" Kathleen replied: "Yes, they could be fitting, always better to just be sure."

According to the PDSA, if a dog suffers a GDV (Gastric dilatation-volvulus), they will likely require surgery to untwist their stomach. However, tragically, even with intervention, some GDVs prove fatal.

Article continues below

The PDSA said: "Any dog can develop a GDV but it's most common in giant and deep chested breeds such as as German Shepherds, Great Danes, Saint Bernards and Dobermanns.

"It's more common in dogs that have a parent or full sibling (brother/sister) that have had a GDV, and tends to mostly affect middle-aged to older dogs."

News.title: US citizens issued 'be prepared' Middle East warning as Donald Trump threatens Iran
News.content:
US citizens issued 'be prepared' Middle East warning as Donald Trump threatens Iran

A new travel advisory has been issued for 10 countries in the Middle East by the US State Department

View Image The US is continuing to strike Iran as the conflict continues (file) (Image: US MARINE CORPS/AFP via Getty Images)

The US has warned its citizens to prepare for a possible evacuation from the Middle East following Donald Trump's latest threat to launch strikes against Iran.

‌



The State Department has issued a fresh advisory covering 10 Middle East countries: the United Arab Emirates (UAE), I srael, Oman, Qatar, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Egypt.

‌



It called on Americans in the region to "exercise heightened vigilance" and "be prepared to depart should there be escalation", while also warning of "flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions", reports the Daily Express.

‌



The advisory mentioned that the "Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted (such as Egypt)".

Posting on X, the alert said: "Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions. Some airlines in the region have postponed resumption of earlier flight schedules; others have cancelled some routes.

‌



"Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation. Americans outside the Middle East should seriously reconsider travel to and through the region.

"Those who do travel to or from the region should monitor information about airport and airline operations. U.S. diplomatic facilities, including outside the Middle East, have been targeted. Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other U.S. interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including U.S. businesses and other institutions."

On Saturday, Major General Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's wartime military command, declared: "The United States is moving at an accelerating pace to fan the flames of a full-scale regional war."

Article continues below

He continued: "It is hereby stated explicitly: Muslim countries must, with foresight, monitor America's crimes and reconsider their cooperation and alignment with the US.

"Otherwise, any country that makes itself a defensive shield for criminal, aggressor America will burn in the fire of war."

News.title: Firefighters battle blaze at Midlands adventure park as public warned to 'avoid area'
News.content:
Firefighters battle blaze at Midlands adventure park as public warned to 'avoid area'

Four crews of firefighters are at the scene tonight, battling a fire in the trees at the popular park

View Image Meriden Adventure Park (Image: Google Maps)

Firefighters are tonight battling a blaze at an adventure play park in the West Midlands. Members of the public have been warned to 'stay away' from Meriden Park in Chelmsley Wood this evening.

‌



The West Midlands Fire Service warned the public about the blaze just before 8.30pm tonight (August 1). Four crews of firefighters are at the scene tonight battling a fire in the trees at the popular park, reports BirminghamLive.

‌



West Midlands Fire Service wrote: "We have four crews in attendance at Meriden Park, Chelmsley Wood, Solihull where they have responded to a fire in the trees. Please avoid the area, where possible."

Article continues below

As well as a large natural lake, and natural woodland, Meriden Adventure Playground is a leading adventure play facility. It has a large children's play area, skate park and football pitch, and is operated by an independent charity.

It hosts a number of community events throughout the year and is popular during the school holidays.

News.title: Family of Nottingham attack victim Barnaby Webber blasts police's 'betrayal of trust'
News.content:
Family of Nottingham attack victim Barnaby Webber blasts police's 'betrayal of trust'

EXCLUSIVE: Ilsadin Skenderaj viewed 12 videos with no policing purpose, including of the victims of the Nottingham attacks being treated by medics and being placed in body bags

View 3 Images Ian Coates, Barnaby Webber and Grace O’Malley Kumar were stabbed to death by Valdo Calocane (Image: PA)

The family of a Nottingham attack victim is horrified by police handling of an officer who accessed distressing bodycam footage of their dead child.

‌



Emma Webber, mother of Barnaby who was killed by Valdo Calocane, feels betrayed after discovering the rogue officer was allowed to quietly quit but was told he had been fired.

‌



Nottingham Police’s deputy chief constable Steve Cooper said Ilsadin Skenderaj had been sacked following a misconduct hearing for looking at the footage with policing purpose.

‌



This was repeated by then-Chief Constable Kate Meynell in a letter to the families of Barnaby and Grace O’Malley Kumar, also fatally stabbed by Calocane in June 2023.

View 3 Images Chief Constable Kate Meynell told the families the officer had been dismissed (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Nottingham Post)

Nottingham killer's brother thought his violent messages were about suicide READ MORE :

But Skenderaj was not dismissed and voluntarily stepped down that September, before the misconduct hearing took place in December.

‌



At home and off duty, Skenderaj viewed 12 separate recordings including of paramedics providing medical assistance to Barnaby and Grace, both aged 19, and placing both in body bags. He was not working on the case.

Ms Webber said: ­“Nottinghamshire Police failed us completely over Special Constable Ilsadin Skenderaj. He watched in detail 12 body-worn videos of my son and his friend being treated – the most private, harrowing moments of their final minutes. The chief constable looked us in the eye and said he had faced disciplinary action and been sacked.

“He [Skenderaj] resigned before any proper consequences could be imposed. They covered it up and kept us in the dark about how extensive the misconduct really was until the public inquiry dragged the truth out.

‌



“It is utterly heartbreaking that such a profound betrayal of trust has been allowed to pass with zero real accountability.”

View 3 Images Barnaby's mum Emma Webber says she feels let down by Nottinghamshire Police (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

University students Barnaby and Grace were walking home from a night out when they were stabbed to death by paranoid schizophrenic Valdo Calocane, who also killed school caretaker Ian Coates, 65, then drove into pedestrians. He is serving an indefinite hospital order.

‌



Skenderaj, who appears to have run a property lettings firm alongside his special constable role, also watched footage from Calocane’s arrest and inside an ambulance. Despite his actions, officers failed to seize his devices and he was allowed to decline a police interview.

Police staff often have access to evidence systems as part of their role, even if they are not assigned to an investigation.

But they are expected to only access information for a legitimate policing purpose. Special constables are part-time, unpaid, volunteer officers. The inquiry into the attacks heard Nottinghamshire Police was ­“reluctant” to investigate how many times staff inappropriately accessed images and footage from that fateful day.

Article continues below

A Nottinghamshire Police spokesman said: “The officer resigned ahead of a gross ­misconduct hearing, which found him guilty in his absence. He therefore would have been dismissed had he not resigned. He was also placed on the police barred list.”

News.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
News.content:
The quickest route for Infantino's exit would be for the Swiss to resign, like his predecessor Sepp Blatter did in 2015.

But Infantino still retains support and he could try to hold out until March, when he is up for re-election for a fourth and final term as president.

What other avenues are open?

The Fifa Council could try to force Infantino's hand through an emergency meeting.

Such a gathering would be triggered if 19 of the 37 Fifa Council members call for one.

Uefa has nine members, AFC has seven, Concacaf five, Africa has six, Conmebol five and Oceania three. It is completed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.

BBC Sport understands there are some doubts that the 19 votes could be achieved.

If they do get to 19, the meeting must take place within two weeks and the Fifa Council could call on Infantino to tender his resignation. But he could simply refuse to do so.

It would, however, add further pressure.

The next step would be an extraordinary congress of the 211 Fifa member associations, which would be held if one-fifth, or 43 associations, "make such a request in writing".

So Uefa, which has 55 nations, can trigger the extraordinary congress whenever it so wishes.

That would take a minimum of two months from the point it is triggered, but more likely three months, and there is no guarantee of success.

In effect, it would be a de facto election without there being another candidate as 106 votes would be needed to pass the vote of no confidence.

Uefa has 55, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

Africa, Conmebol and Oceania have not criticised Infantino's plan.

So could Uefa get to 106? In total, 136 countries officially rejected the investment plan, but voting to reject an idea is not the same as voting to kick Infantino out.

Of the 136, Qatar have already publicly backed him and Mexico have distanced themselves from the joint Concacaf statement.

Which leaves finding a suitable candidate to fight the election in March.

Infantino stood unopposed when he was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 and if someone wants to battle him for the position, the deadline to announce their candidacy is 18 November.

News.title: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say
News.content:
At least three people have been killed and 21 injured after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media quotes security officials as saying.

The blast happened at around 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) on Kudrinskaya square near the city centre.

The National Anti-Terrorist Committee (NAK) said a woman carrying the explosives tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard. The device detonated, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor to the restaurant.

The restaurant, located in one of Moscow's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers, had been holding a private function.

Authorities have not disclosed the guest list or said anything about who they believe was the target of the attack.

Witnesses said they saw people being brought out covered in blood after the explosion.

Initial reports said the blast happened in the establishment's kitchen but the restaurant later issued a statement saying "there was a problem outside".

Roads around the square were briefly closed. Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride through the city but the event was cancelled.

Video released by Russia's RIA news agency showed heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which had been closed off to members of the public.

In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around the Russian capital. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for those attacks.

News.title: Emotional Kerr delivers moment Glasgow 2026 has waited for with men's mile gold
News.content:
There were no pacers. No wave lights. No declarations about what time he would run or what record he would beat. This was a Saturday night scrap - Glasgow rules - and Josh Kerr wasn't going to let anyone beat him in that fight.

Not his childhood pal and Scotland team-mate Jake Wightman. Not the Australian prodigy Cam Myers. Not the former Olympic silver medallist Timothy Cheruiyot.

This Commonwealth Games men's mile was his race, in his country, in front of his people. This gold medal really meant something.

Kerr's explosion of joy after he crossed the line and swaddled himself in a Saltire - having conducted the crowd during his final few strides - made that clear.

And so did his halting attempts to sing along with Flower of Scotland, the 28-year-old repeatedly stopping to bite his lip before wiping away tears from each eye.

"We rush through these moments so quickly," Kerr told BBC Sport Scotland, having spent the best part of 45 minutes doing selfies and signatures. "So I was just telling myself to slow down.

"In my head, I was flashing through all the hard moments and realising that I've come a long way. And to have Flower of Scotland playing versus the GB national anthem, it's just different. Not many times in my career I'll ever have that."

News.title: Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism row defends his work
News.content:
A Cambridge University professor has defended his academic work after finding himself at the centre of a plagiarism row.

The row erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in Prof Jason Arday's work and questioned some of his stated achievements.

While some critics say the treatment of Arday, who is black, has been motivated by racism, others have said the claims of plagiarism were legitimate.

Arday admitted errors in his work, telling the Times, external in an interview on Saturday that he was accountable for those mistakes but that "what I am not is a liar".

He told the newspaper: "There has been, since I arrived at Cambridge, a very well orchestrated and co-ordinated campaign to unseat me from my position."

He argued this was "racially motivated" and that he had become a "lightning rod" for criticism of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policy.

Arday said some errors in his early academic work was because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information, and that similar scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics.

"We're talking about academia here. I didn't murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I've experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable," he told the newspaper.

In 2023, the then 37-year-old sociologist became the youngest ever black professor at Cambridge, telling the BBC at the time his work focused on neurodivergence and race in education.

He was diagnosed with autism and global development delay in his early years, to which his being unable to speak until the age of 11 and unable to read or write until 18 was attributed.

Arday worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at Liverpool John Moores University and going on to teach at Roehampton, Durham and Glasgow.

News.title: I had a vasectomy in my 20s after the trauma of my sons' births
News.content:
Because he was asking for a vasectomy at such a young age, Sam had prepared for the questions his doctor was going to ask him: Don't you think you're too young to know you don't want kids? Could you change your mind in future? You do know reversals are expensive and aren't always successful?

"[The doctor] actually said he had very recently changed his view," says Sam. "And that, if I had come in half a year earlier, he would have turned me away instantly."

His vasectomy took place a couple of months after he first contacted the clinic.

The questions from Sam's doctor were designed to ensure he was making a decision he could live with; men under 30 are more likely to regret a vasectomy, according to guidance from NHS Scotland, external.

Dr Sarah Salkeld, a former GP who is now a medical director for MSI Reproductive Choices, a group of clinics offering various contraceptives to NHS and private patients, says a vasectomy is "very safe and effective".

But she cautions it is important for men to "really think about" whether a vasectomy is right for them.

"We offer everyone counselling to talk about it if they want to, just toâ¦ make sure they've got all the information they need to make that decision."

She says reversals are not routinely available on the NHS as there are strict criteria for having one.

The NHS website points out that other forms of contraception, external are available to men, including condoms and the fertility awareness method - avoiding sex or using condoms on the days when their female partner is most fertile.

Sam told his doctor that, while he loved kids and had a happy childhood himself, he wanted to stay focused on his job as a sound designer for video games.

News.title: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
News.content:
It's a Friday night. A young woman trudges back to her apartment after a day of work. She enters a spotless kitchen, unloads a bag of groceries, and unwraps a frozen pizza before sliding it in the oven.

What follows is a nightly routine that is almost meditative in its mundanity: she lights a candle and gazes briefly at the snow-covered landscape outside her window, piles a premade salad onto a plate with the pizza, and settles on her sofa to eat in front of the TV.

The tagline that accompanies the scene reads: "POV you're a childfree and single girl that has no friends and lives alone so this is how you spend your Friday night."

At the centre of the video â which has amassed seven million views on TikTok â is Lana Isa, a software sales manager in her 20s based in Toronto.

In addition to chronicling her nightly self-care routines, she takes her almost 400,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram on late-night fast food drives, reading sessions perched on a rock by the lake, even a saga of getting locked out of her apartment in the middle of the night.

Isa is part of a growing, albeit niche corner of the internet where content creators, many of them women, share their daily rituals of living alone, choosing to spotlight a lifestyle that prioritises peace and solitude - the antithesis of social media excess.

For Isa, unveiling the "no friends" aspect of her life was less of a tagline, but the "reality" she had been living for several years.

News.title: Does Love Island UK need to pull the US version for a chat?
News.content:
What's your dream Love Island series on paper?

Some watch for the heartwarming romances, like Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury falling for each other back in 2019, while others prefer intense dramas - we see you 2022 winners Ekin-Su CÃ¼lcÃ¼loÄlu and Davide Sanclimenti.

Others tune in for exciting challenges like Snog, Marry, Pie or the ones which literally send heart rates soaring.

For most, it's a mix of all of the above, and it's a balance TV producers have been trying to strike for years with the original UK series, as well as a host of spin-offs and international editions.

It's no secret that Love Island UK linear viewing figures have dropped from their 2019 heyday, with streaming and social media becoming more of a focus.

Across the pond the US edition has been reaching new heights, with the latest eighth series ranked as the number one reality show for five weeks in the States across all streaming platforms, according to its streamer Peacock. , external

It also had an injection of star power as US celebrity fans, including Lizzo, Demi Lovato and Kesha, sent messages of support to the finalists, while rapper Megan Thee Stallion has become a regular guest.

BBC Newsbeat has been speaking to fans, commentators and an ex-Islander to see what they feel the UK edition could learn from the US version to regain its spark.

News.title: Spider-Man fans hail Brand New Day as Holland's best yet
News.content:
Fans have been queuing outside cinemas to catch the latest Spider-Man film, with many hailing it as a spectacular return for the web-slinging superhero.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day marks Tom Holland's fourth standalone adventure as the protagonist and hero Peter Parker.

Picking up after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home, the film follows Parker as he devotes his time to protecting New York City while adjusting to a life in which everyone, including his closest friends, has forgotten who he is.

The fourth Spider-Man film is director Destin Daniel Cretton's second project in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), having previously been at the helm of Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.

Appearing together in the same film for a second time this summer, Holland reprises the role alongside his wife Zendaya, who stars once again as MJ.

There is also a return for Jon Bernthal's Punisher, making his first appearance in an MCU feature film, and an introduction to the MCU for Sadie Sink, whose role in the plot has been kept firmly under wraps.

News.title: Greater Manchester mayor says Burnham's new powers will change lives
News.content:
Greater Manchester's new Mayor Bev Craig has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham's move to give the regions more power could "change our lives".

The Labour candidate claimed victory in Thursday's by-election after securing 309,525 votes over Reform's Sian Astley, who won 157,178.

The 41-year-old will succeed Burnham as mayor, after he stood down to run in the Makerfield by-election in June. The pair appeared together at a Labour rally in Manchester after Craig's election win.

Craig said: "For a prime minister two weeks in, to start giving powers out of Whitehall and putting it in the places that can make a difference - that can change our lives."

She added: "I will rise to his challenge about taking the power and control that he is offering mayors like me to make our regions better.

"Because that is what it is all about."

News.title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche, his company says
News.content:
Purja's death was also confirmed by Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who said that "the tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range of Pakistan, has shocked us".

"The history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring," the prime minister added.

In a statement, Purja's older brother Kamal wrote: "It is with the heaviest heart that I share the devastating news that my beloved younger brother, Nirmal 'Nimsdai' Purja, and the other climbers are no longer with us.

"Although our hearts are broken, we are incredibly proud of you. Your legacy will live forever," he added.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme that Purja had led many expeditions that she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Kiani said the Alpine Club would only announce his death once the body has been recovered - but she added that "we are fearing them all dead".

She also said rescuers had seen some bodies - but were yet to reach them.

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit after an avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised that if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted," he wrote.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

News.title: William and Kate bring children to second last day of Commonwealth Games
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have brought their three children to watch some of the final sporting events at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Cheering crowds at the city's OVO Hydro were treated to exhilarating performances in the netball semi-finals where the family watched New Zealand's 61-54 win over England.

Known as the Duke and Duchess of Rothesay while in Scotland, the couple also spent time meeting athletes, staff and volunteers during a slightly blustery visit to the venue on the River Clyde.

They then made their way to the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome - where they chatted to British cyclist Dame Laura Kenny and sat one row behind another Olympic cycling champion, Sir Chris.

News.title: Manhunt after prisoner escapes from van outside court
News.content:
A manhunt is under way after a prisoner escaped from a van taking him to a court appearance.

Stephen Grzyb, 22, was being transported by contractor GEOAmey from Belle Vale custody suite to Liverpool Magistrates' Court to face burglary charges on Saturday.

As the van arrived outside the court building, at around 10:00 BST, Grzyb was able to flee and ran off down Red Cross Street towards the Strand.

Merseyside Police said: "Assisting him in any way will bring police to your own door, so it is not an association worth keeping."

News.title: Suffolk fire 'stable' and fundraiser set up
News.content:
The blaze that has devastated heathland in Suffolk is now "stable" but crews have continued to tackle hotspots on what is the fourth day since the flames took hold.

The fire affecting RSPB Minsmere and Dunwich Heath started at about 17:00 BST on Wednesday and engulfed 371 acres (150 hectares) at its height - equivalent to the size of 210 football pitches.

Wildlife habitats of some of the UK's rarest species have been destroyed.

The National Trust has launched a fundraiser to help the habitats "recover and thrive in a changing climate".

Meanwhile, some local people have started returning to normal life.

A scheduled market went ahead at nearby Westleton earlier, which an organiser said was the chance for people to take their minds off recent events.

News.title: Soap star Shane Richie facing drink-drive charge
News.content:
EastEnders actor Shane Richie is to appear in court charged with drink-driving, police have said.

Essex Police confirmed it was called to reports of a suspected drink-driver in the Church Langley Way area of Harlow, shortly before 23:20 BST on Wednesday.

A force spokesman confirmed the 62-year-old, of Tadworth, Surrey, was arrested and a charge of drink-driving had been authorised against him.

It added Richie, real name Shane Roche, was due to appear at Colchester Magistrates' Court on 9 September.

Richie plays Alfie Moon in EastEnders, making his first appearance in the BBC soap in 2002.

The Sun reported he was arrested, external at a Tesco petrol station forecourt.

Essex Police said: "Officers were called to reports of a suspected drink-driver in the area of Church Langley Way, Harlow, shortly before 23:20 on Wednesday, 29 July.

"On arrival, officers arrested a man.

"A charge of drink-driving has subsequently been authorised against Shane Roche, 62, of Tadworth, Surrey."

Richie's representative has been contacted for comment.

Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below.

News.title: Peak District's rebrand deal brings in cash - but also criticism
News.content:
A deal between Peak District bosses and car firm Skoda to put up temporary signs welcoming tourists to "the Peaq District" in honour of the firm's new electric model has given the park authority's coffers a welcome boost.

However, it has also sparked protests from campaigners and residents unhappy about the commercial aspect of the arrangement.

One campaigner said: "If national parks are prepared to sell their very name to the highest bidder, then we're already on the path to industrial extraction of the most protected landscapes."

Park bosses have defended the "fantastic" deal and said the partnership brought in extra funds for conservation and heritage work.

With national parks continuing to grapple with funding pressures, could the partnership be a sign of things to come for the Peak District and beyond?

News.title: Boaters race against clock as drained canals close
News.content:
Boaters are racing against the clock to beat canal closures as waterways run dry due to extreme heat.

Some channels connecting large parts of the Midlands and the North of England have lost several inches of water, leaving narrowboats stuck and those already on the canals facing being stranded miles from home for weeks on end.

Campaigner George Seward said he was getting up at 05:00 BST and cruising until dark to get his narrowboat through the Atherstone flight of locks, after a sudden closure was announced.

"They're unlikely to be open again for many weeks and I want to make sure I get through that flight so I can get my boat safely home," he said.

The locks on the Coventry Canal in Warwickshire are due to shut on Tuesday morning, with last entry on Monday afternoon, as the Canal and River Trust (CRT) tries to conserve dwindling supplies.

For Seward, who is Midlands regional chair of the Association of Waterways Cruising Clubs, the deadline is the difference between getting his boat home to Hinckley in Leicestershire and being potentially marooned for an unspecified period.

News.title: Idaho shooting updates: At least 3 dead and 2 injured in mass shooting at Idaho In-N-Out with casualties expected ‘to increase’
News.content:

At least three people were killed and two others were injured in a mass shooting at an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, according to police and local officials.

The suspected shooter, whose identity has not been revealed, is dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said during a press conference.

The number of victims is expected to increase, Joshua Palmer, a public information coordinator for the city, told The Independent.

“We want to emphasize that that number may change,” Palmer said. “That was just the first number we got.”

An “active shooter incident” was first reported at 2:29 p.m. Soon afterward, police urged people to avoid the area, noting that roads in the area would be closed, as officers responded.

Shelter in place orders have since been lifted, Palmer said.

This is a breaking story...

Police say multiple people died in a shooting at a southern Idaho In-N-Out fast food restaurant, and others were injured.

The shooter is also dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said.

The shooting was reported Saturday afternoon near a busy shopping area in Twin Falls.

Hicks said he did not have a number yet of how many were killed and injured. Officials were still in the process of notifying next of kin.

THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. AP’s earlier story follows below.

TWIN FALLS, Idaho (AP) — A shooting near a southern Idah shopping center left multiple people injured Saturday afternoon, authorities reported.

Twin Falls County Commissioner Brent Reinke said Sheriff Jack Johnson told him five people were hurt in the shooting, which started at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant.

While there were no immediate confirmations of deaths and details remained limited, Reinke said it was likely there were some fatalities. He added that the shooter “is also down.”

Reinke, who is also former prison chief for the Idaho Department of Corrections, said he learned of the incident just before 4 p.m. Multiple agencies responded.

“We’re loading people up, all the witnesses, and taking them to different locations for interviews,” Reinke said. “We should have a lot more information within the hour.”

Twin Falls police advised people to avoid the area as they closed roads.

St. Luke’s Magic Valley spokesperson Taylor Marschner said in a statement that the medical center was “working closely with law enforcement and emergency responders as they manage the situation.”

Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is about 130 miles (205 kilometers) southeast of Boise and about 75 miles (120 kilometers) north of the Nevada border.

Three people have died and at least 21 more are injured after a homemade bomb carried by a woman exploded near a central Moscow restaurant on Saturday evening, Russian authorities said.

The explosion, which occurred at around 7:55pm local time (5:55pm BST), exploded near an upscale Italian restaurant located in one of Moscow's seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinkskaya Square, police said.

Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee said that an unidentified woman had tried to get ​into ⁠the restaurant but was ‌stopped by a security guard, Russian news agencies reported.

open image in gallery Law enforcement officers stand guard at the site of an explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow ( REUTERS )

Among the dead were the security guard, the unnamed woman, and another visitor, the committee added. They have not been named and there are no official theories about the perpetrator. Those injured had received wounds of varying seriousness, according to police.

The Kommersant daily newspaper cited sources as saying that the bomb had been intended to maim and kill guests who were enjoying themselves on the restaurant's summer terrace outside. The restaurant's ‌website said the venue had ​been closed on Saturday for a private event, but it is unclear who was present.

More than four years into a full-scale war with Ukraine, Russia's FSB security service said earlier this year that authorities would step up protection for high-ranking military officials after a series of assassinations and attempted killings it blamed on Kyiv.

open image in gallery Law enforcement officers and emergency services personnel work at the site of an explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow ( Reuters )

In June, Vladimir Putin’s ammunition chief Damir Davydov was killed in a car bombing in Moscow.

But there has not yet been any suggestion that Saturday’s attack was linked to the Ukraine war with Moscow’s officials still to put forward any theories.

Russia's state RIA news agency released video of heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which had been closed off to the public.

open image in gallery Police vehicles at the site of an explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow ( REUTERS )

Russian state TV earlier speculated that the explosion may have been caused by a gas canister detonating, a theory which was later dropped.

Investigators and emergency services remain working at the scene.

The Baza online news outlet, which has good contacts with law enforcement, said the explosion had occurred at the upscale Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant.

The top general overseeing U.S. forces in Europe reportedly warned the Pentagon this week that he does not have enough resources to continue protecting Israel from incoming ballistic missiles.

Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, the commander of the U.S. European Command, wrote to senior military officials at the Pentagon that unless another Navy destroyer is deployed, he would have to choose between defending the homeland over Israel, the Washington Post reported Saturday.

The U.S. currently has five destroyers based out of port in Spain to deploy to the eastern Mediterranean Sea to help defend Israel. A sixth vessel is expected to be added later this year, the Washington Post reported.

But five months into President Donald Trump’s war with Iran, the ongoing fighting has taken a toll on the military assets, requiring more maintenance for the destroyers in addition to utilizing missiles.

The Independent has asked the Pentagon for comment.

open image in gallery Gen Alexus Grynkewich, who leads the US European Command, warned the Pentagon this week that he would no longer be able to defend Israel without more military resources ( Getty )

Since the collapse of a U.S.-Iran ceasefire in early July, the U.S. has reinstated a naval blockade on Iranian ports, further straining the capacity of the Navy.

Several vessels, including aircraft carriers and at least 11 destroyers, have been deployed closer to Iran to assist in the blockade and also ensure the safe passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

The destroyers used in the Mediterranean Sea to defend Israel have been deployed to do so for several years. The vessels are armed with an array of missiles and radar systems to track and take down incoming threats – both from Iran and from the Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen.

As of Friday, two destroyers were in the Mediterranean Sea while three others were at the port in Spain, a U.S. official told the Washington Post.

The on-and-off-again fighting between the U.S. and adversaries has taken a toll on the U.S. military for months.

In May, the Washington Post reported that a Defense Department assessment found that the U.S. depleted more of its military’s advanced missile-defense interceptors while defending Israel than Israeli forces had.

open image in gallery Trump’s war with Iran has strained US Navy resources, with multiple vessels deployed near Iran amid the ongoing Strait of Hormuz tensions as well as other deployed to help defend Israel ( US Navy )

Not only have military assets dwindled, but at least 18 service members have been killed, igniting domestic ire about the president’s war with Iran.

The war is largely unpopular and becoming more disliked, even by members of Trump’s MAGA movement, as it drives everyday prices up for Americans because of transportation issues in the Strait of Hormuz.

Even members of Congress have seemingly grown weary of the U.S. exuding its resources for the Iran war – and particularly toward Israel.

In mid-July, nearly half of House Democrats voted in favor of eliminating billions of dollars of aid to Israel. Although the measure ultimately failed, the number of Democrats indicates lawmakers are less enthusiastic about supporting a longtime U.S. ally.

Chancellor John Healey has said he will be “watching closely” to protect the public from price gouging at the petrol pump and in supermarkets as the war in Iran continues to hit prices.

Mr Healey conceded that “we can’t completely stop the squeeze” on families and businesses, amid prime minister Andy Burnham’s efforts to show he will focus on tackling the cost of living since taking office two weeks ago.

But he signalled he would be ready to intervene to protect consumers from unfair price rises at home.

“We’ll be watching closely for any suggestions that customers are being taken for a ride at the pump or the till.

“Companies’ willingness to work with the Government throughout this crisis has been positive, and there has been no significant evidence of so-called price gouging, but I want to be blunt in reassuring the public that our regulators have the powers to clamp down on it if it happens,” Mr Healey wrote in The Telegraph.

The former defence secretary said he had spoken to international counterparts in his first days as chancellor about their joint economic response to the ongoing war in Iran.

Mr Healey said: “Being frank, we can’t completely stop the squeeze that families and businesses will feel with a global shock of this scale.”

“What we can do is be an active, hands-on Government that puts British interests first – giving breathing space to those feeling financial strain and making our country more resilient so we can better weather these shocks in the future.”

The start of Mr Burnham’s premiership has seen him announce a succession of measures aimed at alleviating cost-of-living pressures, such as a cut in VAT on energy bills and capping bus fares at £2 throughout 2027.

The prime minister reiterated on Sunday that he would like to take further action to bring down utility bills and rail fares.

“I think rail fares are too high, outrageously so in some instances. So that’s something that’s in my sights.

“I mentioned VAT and electricity bills. It’s a short-term measure at this moment, but let’s see where we can go with that,” he told the Sunday Mirror.

The raft of measures Mr Burnham has unveiled, including cutting business rates for pubs and an expansion of technical training in schools, are likely to require additional spending.

Mr Healey promised that his first budget would be “built on fiscal discipline” as he revealed this week that it would take place on October 28.

He and the Prime Minister have written to the Cabinet to make clear there is no new money coming for the fresh pledges, he told The Times.

Departments need to be ready to “shift funding away from unproductive or legacy programmes that no longer reflect this administration’s priorities”, he wrote in the letter.

Joe Rogan said that there is “no clear way” to end Donald Trump’s ongoing war with Iran, which he called an “unprovoked attack” by the United States.

The popular podcaster made the remarks during an episode of his show, released on Friday, with Annie Jacobsen, an investigative journalist, who was brought on to discuss her new book, Biological War: A Scenario.

After discussing the government’s handling of Covid-19 and the possibility of future pandemics, Rogan turned to the conflict in the Middle East, which has now dragged on for five months with no clear end in sight.

“How much does this Iran thing freak you out?” the comedian asked Jacobsen, who has written multiple books about the U.S. military.

Jacobsen called the war “terrible,” "unnecessary" and the opposite of what the Department of Defense was designed for. She then pointed to a “big shift” that occurred during the Iraq war, which she said left soldiers feeling “used” and led to “a fundamental warping of what the military is.”

open image in gallery Joe Rogan said that there's 'no clear way' to end the Iran war, which he called an 'unprovoked attack' by the United States ( The Joe Rogan Experience, YouTube )

“Yeah, without a doubt,” Rogan responded. “And also no clear way to resolve this at all. And it seems like our stockpiles are running dry…bases are getting blown up by drones.”

Both the host and guest also lamented what they described as coverage of the war that has focused on its financial cost — rather than its human toll.

To date, 18 U.S. service members have been killed and hundreds have been wounded, the Pentagon has said. President Donald Trump has framed the American death toll in the war — which he says is necessary to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon — as relatively low compared to past conflicts.

As of March, 3,636 people have been killed in Iran, nearly half of whom were civilians, Reuters reported, citing human rights group HRANA.

open image in gallery To date, 18 U.S. service members have been killed and hundreds have been wounded, the Pentagon has said. Pictured: Trump salutes at a dignified transfer of the remains of deceased service members on July 22 ( AFP via Getty Images )

“And also the real problem is it makes America an enemy,” Rogan continued. “And it makes us less safe because America has done this thing — this unprovoked attack — and so now they have a reason to attack back.”

Multiple recent polls indicate many Americans are on the same page. In an AP-NORC survey released last month, nearly two-thirds of respondents said the conflict has not been worth fighting.

Rogan, one of the world’s most popular podcasters, endorsed Trump on the eve of the 2024 election.

Since Trump returned to office, the comedian has openly criticized him on multiple occasions, including over his immigration crackdown and the Epstein files. During an interview with JD Vance earlier this month, the vice president admitted the administration had “mishandled” the release of the files.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Kerr wins by a mile: Scot claims Commonwealth gold to emulate Bannister
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.
