World.title: Turkish Air Force takes over NATO's newly upgraded Baltic air defense mission in Estonia
World.content:
Turkey's air force has been deployed to Estonia for the first time to participate in NATO's newly transformed Baltic air defense mission and will patrol the airspace for the next four months.

At last month's NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, it was decided that the two-decade-old Baltic air policing monitoring mission in Estonia and Lithuania would evolve into an air defense mission from August 1.

The new mission makes it possible to counter aerial attacks by employing NATO's integrated air defense system.

"This should ensure that if, for example, the threat picture changes and there is a need to rapidly bring in additional forces, that will be done. Likewise, all the necessary pre-authorizations for making all possible decisions have already been completed as far in advance as possible," Minister of Defense Hanno Pevkur (Reform) said on Friday.

The four-month rotation timetable for NATO allies has already been agreed upon for the next three years. The minister said air forces are unlikely to get bored, as few regions have similar conditions.

The Turkish Air force will lead the first rotation of the Baltic Air Defense Mission in Estonia from August 1, 2026. Source: EDF/ Siim Verner Teder

"Under previous practice, once, twice, even three times a week they have to go and identify aircraft from a country that is not friendly toward us. In their home countries, as a rule, and if we are talking primarily about, for example, Portugal or Spain, which have served here, or Germany as well, they do not have to constantly identify Russian reconnaissance aircraft or Russian fighter jets flying nearby. The visual contact you get with a Russian fighter jet is not something you can experience in Portugal. Therefore, every country that comes here is certainly in a somewhat special situation," Pevkur told ERR.

The Turkish Air Force contingent at Ämari consists of nearly 80 personnel, including 10 pilots. Five F-16 fighter jets are on round-the-clock standby for takeoff.

"Of course, we are proud to be here under NATO. Our aim and goal is to protect NATO airspace, identify threats in this region, and maintain strong air deterrence," Turkish Air Force pilot Lieutenant Atila Özdemir said.

On Friday, mission medals were awarded to the Portuguese Air Force personnel who flew the last air policing mission in Baltic airspace. Lt. Col. Katrin Tõugjas, commander of the Ämari Air Base, thanked the Portuguese for their "outstanding cooperation" and welcomed the new Turkish contingent.

The Turkish Air Force's deployment will end in November. The Italians took over the mission in Lithuania.

The Turkish Air force will lead the first rotation of the Baltic Air Defense Mission in Estonia from August 1, 2026. Source: EDF/ Siim Verner Teder

World.title: Chevron CFO bullish on Iraq after West Qurna 2, Nassiriya agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chevron boasts “significant potential” to expand its activities in Iraq over the next decade, according to Chief Financial Officer Eimear Bonner, highlighting the US oil company’s increasing trust in the country’s energy sector after recent deals with Baghdad.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Bonner said that Iraq remained one of Chevron’s top priority markets for future production expansion after the signing of preliminary agreements to pursue negotiations on the massive West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya oil fields.

She added that Chevron has been encouraged by its interaction with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Iraq’s Ministry of Oil while discussions continue and that the corporation is also collaborating with Baghdad on diverse crude export routes to boost Iraq’s long-term energy security.

The statements bolster rising trust among foreign energy corporations after Al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States earlier this month, during which Iraq inked more than $60 billion in investment deals covering energy, infrastructure, banking, and technology.

World.title: Syria joins Saudi Arabia, Jordan in warning Iraq over Iran-backed militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Syria has joined Saudi Arabia and Jordan in warning Baghdad that strikes conducted from Iraqi soil against neighboring nations may result in military strikes against the armed groups responsible, according to Syrian military officials cited by regional media.

According to Al Jazeera and the US-funded Al Hurra, a senior Syrian military source said that Damascus will react to any strikes from Iraq by attacking the “terrorist militias” involved inside Iraqi territory.

The purported warning comes amid a steep increase in regional tensions after US-Saudi bombings against Iran-backed militias in Iraq in retaliation for drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were conducted from Iraqi territory.

The Iraqi government has frequently said that it would not allow Iraqi land to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighboring nations.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi recently issued an order establishing a comprehensive security strategy aimed at enhancing state authority and preventing armed organizations from endangering regional security.

The new threat puts further pressure on Baghdad, as more neighboring nations indicate they may take direct action if cross-border assaults continue.

Iraqi authorities have attempted to prevent such a situation, claiming that security activities should be overseen by the Iraqi government rather than foreign forces.

Several Iran-backed organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are at the heart of the conflict, including Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security system, some of its sections have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and have been accused by regional governments of carrying out strikes outside of Baghdad’s jurisdiction.

For Iraq, the diplomatic stakes go beyond security.

Baghdad has been attempting to reestablish ties with Syria as part of greater regional economic integration, including talks on resurrecting the old Iraq-Syria oil pipeline to the Mediterranean, which is considered strategically crucial for diversifying Iraq’s export routes outside the Gulf.

The purported Syrian warning comes at a critical moment for Al-Zaidi’s administration, which has spent recent months bolstering relations with Washington, Ankara, Riyadh, and Damascus while portraying Iraq as a secure destination for global investment.

The mounting threats from neighboring Arab governments highlight the importance of Baghdad demonstrating its ability to prevent armed groups from conducting strikes independent of the state.

Failure to do so risks increasing regional military tensions and jeopardizing Iraq’s aspirations to boost commerce, energy cooperation, and infrastructure projects with its neighbors.

The Syrian government has not issued an official warning, and IraqiNews.com has not independently confirmed the statements ascribed to the Syrian military source.

However, the claims reflect rising regional worry that strikes by Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil could further destabilize the area and hamper Iraq’s diplomatic and economic goals.

World.title: Iran-backed militias threaten Iraq’s ties with US and Gulf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Escalating tensions between Iran-backed militias are providing one of the most serious hurdles yet to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s ambitions to deepen ties with the United States and Gulf states while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

The most recent crisis followed US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, when Saudi Arabia accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones at oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Riyadh claimed that the operation targeted the militias responsible for the assaults rather than the Iraqi state or its military forces, but Baghdad denounced the strikes as a breach of national sovereignty.

The recent tensions are being fueled by numerous prominent Iran-aligned organizations operating inside Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), notably Kataib Hezbollah, Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada.

While the PMF is technically part of Iraq’s security apparatus, many of its groups have strong links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and have occasionally conducted operations outside of Baghdad’s chain of command.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi responded by calling an emergency meeting of the Ministerial Council for National Security, canceling a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and announcing a comprehensive security strategy to prevent Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring countries.

The administration also reiterated its resolve to keep all weapons entirely under state control.

That vow has gained importance after Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington earlier this month, during which Iraq and the United States reiterated their commitment to completing the US-led coalition operation by the end of September 2026.

During the visit, Al-Zaidi pledged to ensure that all weapons eventually come into the control of the Iraqi state, citing it as a cornerstone of his government’s security strategy and a crucial step toward bolstering Iraq’s sovereignty and stability.

Since entering office, Al-Zaidi has maintained a policy of balancing Iraq’s ties with rival regional and international forces.

During recent travels to Washington, Ankara, and Tehran, he achieved huge investment and cooperation deals totaling tens of billions of dollars in the energy, banking, technology, infrastructure, and industrial sectors.

His administration has also attempted to strengthen connections with Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and other Gulf nations via new transportation corridors, energy alliances, and trade agreements aimed at diversifying Iraq’s economy beyond oil and positioning the country as a regional center linking the Gulf to Europe.

According to analysts, Baghdad’s approach is highly dependent on proving that the Iraqi state, rather than armed groups, controls the country’s security and foreign policy.

Continued strikes from Iraqi territory risk eroding the country’s reputation with major regional allies and international investors, at a time when foreign investment has risen after years of turmoil.

The stakes rose when US President Donald Trump said that recent US-Saudi operations against Iran-backed militias were coordinated with the Iraqi government, a claim Baghdad has denied.

Observers believe it reflects rising discontent among Iraq’s leadership with armed groups accused of dragging the nation into regional conflicts that contradict Baghdad’s diplomatic and economic interests.

Al-Zaidi is currently facing the most significant test of his leadership.

Delivering on his promise to place all weapons under state control will be critical not only for Iraq’s internal security but also for maintaining trust with the United States, Gulf Arab states, and international investors, many of whom support many of the country’s largest economic projects.

Baghdad’s dilemma now extends beyond managing ties between Washington and Tehran.

It demonstrates that the Iraqi state possesses both the authority and the political will to prevent Iran-backed militias from using Iraqi territory to launch attacks that risk isolating the country, harming relations with Arab neighbors and the United States, and jeopardizing Iraq’s long-term economic recovery and investment goals.

World.title: Iraq faces growing fiscal strain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is under increasing financial strain as plummeting oil earnings tighten government budgets, with Health Minister Abdul Hussein al-Mousawi saying that ensuring monthly public-sector wages has become the government’s top priority.

Speaking at a public meeting, al-Mousawi stated that the government requires approximately 10.8 trillion Iraqi dinars ($8.2 billion) per month to pay public-sector salaries, while current monthly oil revenues have fallen to approximately 2.5 trillion dinars, highlighting the growing gap between government obligations and income.

The statements are one of the most direct public acknowledgements by a top Iraqi official of the government’s financial challenges after months of decreased oil prices and fewer export profits.

Iraq’s government finances remain very vulnerable to variations in global energy markets because the vast bulk of public revenue comes from crude oil.

Official figures published this week indicated that oil accounted for over 84% of federal income in the first five months of 2026, but collections decreased by more than one-third compared to the same time the previous year as oil prices and export profits plummeted.

The health minister also warned of financing restrictions in the healthcare sector, citing worries about the supply of medications and the government’s capacity to sustain public services if financial pressures continue.

The fresh warnings follow weeks of increased regional tensions, which disrupted oil markets and added uncertainty to Iraq’s economic prospects.

As OPEC’s second-largest producer, Iraq relies on oil exports to fund wages, pensions, social welfare, and the majority of government expenditure, making the budget susceptible to long-term reductions in crude prices.

Economists have long cautioned that Iraq’s reliance on oil income makes the nation susceptible to external shocks, while a hefty public-sector pay bill constrains the government’s budgetary flexibility.

Previous administrations attempted to diversify income streams via tax changes and non-oil investments, but hydrocarbons remain the economy’s backbone.

The financial pressure comes at a critical time for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government, which has been promoting Iraq as a destination for billions of dollars in foreign investment following agreements signed with US, Turkish, and international companies in energy, banking, technology, and infrastructure.

Continued budgetary strain may make it more urgent to accelerate economic reforms, raise non-oil income, and improve public financial management to lessen Iraq’s reliance on petroleum exports.

They also emphasize that preserving investor trust will be contingent on the government’s ability to maintain macroeconomic stability while continuing to fund big development projects.

Despite the present issues, Iraq has large foreign currency reserves, which act as a financial cushion for the government.

However, experts warn that while reserves might help absorb short-term shocks, they are not a substitute for the fundamental changes needed to diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on unpredictable oil earnings.

World.title: Iraq expects record 22 million pilgrims for Arbaeen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is prepared to welcome around 22 million pilgrims for this year’s Arbaeen pilgrimage, including up to 5 million overseas tourists, in what officials believe to be one of the country’s greatest religious gatherings and a significant boost to tourism and the local economy.

According to Iraqi official data, well over 22 million people are anticipated to attend the annual pilgrimage to the holy city of Karbala, with 4.5 million to 5 million pilgrims coming from outside Iraq.

The government has announced that tens of thousands of volunteers would be deployed to assist pilgrims, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has urged officials to boost the number of buses and other transport services to facilitate travel during the festival.

The surge of foreign tourists is projected to have a substantial impact on Iraq’s tourism, hospitality, transportation, and retail industries, with hotels, restaurants, transit operators, and local businesses benefitting from increased demand during the pilgrimage season.

Officials have extended transportation networks in preparation for this year’s pilgrimage, including more rail services, buses, and logistical assistance, as part of larger measures to boost connectivity and promote Iraq’s tourist industry.

The government has increasingly highlighted religious tourism as a crucial pillar of economic diversification, with millions of people visiting the country’s holy sites at Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra each year.

According to officials, continuing investment in infrastructure and tourist services will help Iraq become one of the Middle East’s major religious tourism destinations, while also creating jobs and helping local economies around the country.

World.title: Reports: Iraq PM threatened to resign over militia disarmament
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has threatened to resign if Iran-aligned armed groups do not cooperate with his government’s efforts to bring all weapons under state control, according to reports citing political sources, highlighting the growing pressure on Baghdad to address one of its most difficult security challenges.

According to sources, Al-Zaidi warned leaders of Iraq’s Shi’ite Coordination Framework that if armed groups did not react to government efforts to disarm and completely submit to state authority, he would stand down.

IraqiNews.com was unable to independently verify the claims, and the Prime Minister’s office had no immediate response.

According to the sources, Al-Zaidi has been more dissatisfied by what he sees as a lack of cooperation on one of his administration’s fundamental commitments: guaranteeing that all weapons stay solely under the control of the Iraqi government.

The claims came days after US-Saudi airstrikes struck Iran-backed groups in Iraq in response to drone assaults on Saudi oil installations, which Riyadh said were launched from Iraqi territory.

The bombings forced Al-Zaidi to call an emergency security conference, cancel a planned trip to Saudi Arabia, and unveil a new security strategy aimed at preventing Iraqi territory from being used to launch attacks on neighboring nations.

Armed organizations have emerged as one of Al-Zaidi’s most pressing problems.

Since entering office, he has attempted to solicit billions of dollars in foreign investment with trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara, while portraying Iraq as a stable location for oil, infrastructure, and technological projects.

Analysts believe Baghdad’s economic objectives are strongly dependent on its ability to show that the state, not armed groups, controls Iraq’s security strategy.

Repeated strikes conducted from Iraqi territory have strained ties with regional allies and risk weakening investor trust.

According to Western diplomatic sources published by Asharq Al-Awsat, key Iraqi officials, including Al-Zaidi and members of Iraq’s security apparatus, have received threats in connection with the government’s attempts to restrict weaponry outside of state control.

Unlike many regional leaders, Iraq’s prime minister leads by wide political agreement rather than a legislative majority, restricting his power to make unilateral choices.

Major security and political changes usually need agreement among Iraq’s different political blocs.

Al-Zaidi’s biggest power may not be the threat of resignation, but rather the international backing his administration has garnered as a result of recent accords with the United States, Turkey, and other allies.

These agreements, which span energy, finance, technology, and infrastructure, have boosted hopes that Iraq will attract tens of billions of dollars in investment if security improves.

Whether Al-Zaidi can translate that international momentum into domestic reforms will ultimately depend on gaining broader political support for his pledge to keep all weapons under Iraqi state control, which has become one of his government’s most closely watched tests.

World.title: Iraq denies launching strikes from its territory against neighboring nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The military spokesperson for the Iraqi commander-in-chief, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed on Thursday that neither a foreign nor local body has presented proof that recent regional drone attacks were launched from Iraqi territory.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Numan urged accusing parties to submit reliable proof, saying that Baghdad has yet to receive such data.

The development comes following statements made by the Saudi Ministry of Defense, alleging that drone attacks targeting key oil infrastructure in the past few days originated in Iraq.

The Iraqi official indicated that the government will neither tolerate unilateral military acts from within its borders nor accept foreign violations of its territorial sovereignty.

Al-Numan’s remarks come a day after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting several bases of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), killing and injuring many fighters.

The joint operation targeted several logistical and weapons storage locations in different provinces in Iraq, escalating the current regional battle.

The PMF described the joint US-Saudi strike as a dangerous escalation and a clear breach of Iraqi sovereignty.

World.title: Iraqi oil flows to continue via Turkey’s Ceyhan as renewal deal is discussed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkish sources told Reuters that crude oil shipments from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan will continue while the two countries seek an arrangement to extend the pipeline’s operation for another 12 months.

On July 27, a bilateral agreement that had been in place for decades ended. Despite expectations, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi did not sign a 12-month renewal deal during his meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Tuesday.

According to a Turkish official, oil flows via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline, which is Baghdad’s only operational export pipeline, will continue while negotiations for a renewal deal are still in progress.

Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar recently announced a 12-month extension agreement between the two countries.

During a joint press conference in Ankara, Erdogan stated on Tuesday that Turkey hopes to finalize a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement as soon as possible.

An extension is intended to provide additional time for discussions on a complete accord. Turkey aims to fully utilize the 1.5 million barrels per day pipeline and consider expanding it to oil fields in southern Iraq.

Turkish data suggests that the pipeline currently transports approximately 170,000 barrels per day.

These extended hours without adequate rest led to physical and mental exhaustion, negatively impacting their performance and health,â commission said, referring to the report.Doctorsâ organisation âUnited Doctors Frontâ had approached the court demanding healthy working conditions, pointing out that cases of doctorsâ suicides are on the rise and claiming that 150 such cases have been reported in five years.

NEW DELHI: Review committees of Railway Board have recommended premature retirement of five Group âAâ officers in âpublic interestâ, a decision which officials said was aimed at sending out a strong message of âzero tolerance for corruption, lack of integrity and inefficiencyâ.

While two of these officers belong to senior administrative grade (SAG), being equivalent to joint secretary-level officers, the other three are junior administrative grade (JAG) railway officers, who are at director or joint director level. âIntegrity, discipline and accountability in public service remain non-negotiable. It said the review committees had carried out detailed assessment of the officersâ service records in accordance with prescribed procedure. MUMBAI: CBI lodged a cheating case against Reliance Capital Ltd (RCL), its ex-chairman Anil Ambani and unknown public servants in the alleged Rs 1,816 crore loss caused to Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).CBI alleged that EPFO invested Rs 2,500 crore in RCLâs secured non-convertible debentures in 2013-14 and the company subsequently defaulted on repayment.Earlier, the issue was settled before National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), but recently ED shared its investigation finding of RCLâs fraudulent transactions. Based on this, EPFO subsequently filed a fraud case with CBI against Ambani and RCL.A spokesperson of Anil Ambani said, âThe FIR registered by CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. The remaining amount of Rs 1,007 crore, along with Rs 809 crore interest, remained unpaid.ED, which probed RCL in a separate case, recently shared its findings with EPFO.EPFO said in its complaint to CBI that âthe conduct of and transactions entered into Reliance Capital Limited and the persons in charge of its management during the period 7 Dec 2019 to 6 Dec 2021 disclose various fraudulent transactions...â

World.title: Monsoon hope as WMO sees an El Niño counter
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Monsoon may avoid deficient phase with positive IOD

NEW DELHI: The risk of overall monsoon rainfall being âbelow normalâ continues to loom over India due to a strengthening El NiÃ±o, but World Meteorological Organisationâs (WMO) latest monthly global seasonal climate update, released late Friday night, offered a ray of hope. It predicted the possibility of a âpositiveâ Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), which could offset to an extent the negative impact of El NiÃ±o.El NiÃ±o is a climatic pattern of warming of surface waters of central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean and is associated with a weak monsoon and harsher summer in India. IOD, on the other hand, has to do with the difference in sea surface temperatures between western and eastern parts of tropical Indian Ocean. It helps in formation of stronger monsoon winds.âA positive IOD is expected to develop... Combined with exceptionally warm global oceans and the likelihood of a positive IOD, the developing El NiÃ±o is expected to shape weather patterns across many parts of the world in the months ahead,â WMO said.If WMOâs forecast comes true, there is a possibility of improved rainfall conditions in south peninsular India â the region which had reported a high cumulative rainfall deficit of 22% as of Aug 1 â in particular and over many parts of the country in general.It may prevent India from slipping from âbelow normalâ phase to âdeficientâ monsoon phase at the end of the rainy season.El NiÃ±o Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and IOD are two key factors that govern variation in monsoon rainfall. Though IMD Friday flagged the continuation of âneutralâ IOD conditions through the remaining period of southwest (summer) monsoon, it, at the same time, referred to climate forecasts from some international forecasting centres suggesting that positive IOD conditions are likely to develop during Sept.

World.title: Judge Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
World.content:
NEW DELHI: SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan has questioned opacity in the collegiumâs decisions on judicial appointments.

âI have noticed that the last three collegium resolutions contain no reasons whatsoever.

Is this a step back from the principle of transparency?â said Justice Bhuyan at a panel discussion on Saturday.

âBy withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as âantsâ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional,â he said.

Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: Bhuyan

To prevent the entry of such people, âthere should be some discussion, there should be some reasons givenâ, said Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.

Though the judge didnât name anyone, the comment was an apparent reference to a remark by an Allahabad high court judge at a social event in 2024.

He was speaking at the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index: Assessing Disclosure of Information by the Supreme Court and the High Courts, prepared by the Justice, Access and Lowering Delays in India (JALDI) Initiative at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy.

The judge stressed that deliberations on the elevation and transfer of judges by the SC collegium largely remain confidential, contrary to the principle of judicial transparency.





âWhile carrying out the next assessment on the scale of Judicial Transparency Index, I may request the JALDI team to also look into the aspect of opacity of the collegium system. Deliberations on elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential. Reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full. And the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly disclosed instrument. It is a very important issue.

Citizens have a right to know what is happening in the courts. They have a right to know who would be their judges.

They have a right to know judgments. These should be in the public domainâ, Justice Bhuyan underlined.

The report is the first systematic study assessing transparency practices across Indiaâs higher judiciary and evaluates disclosure of information by the Supreme Court and high courts across judicial processes, institutional governance and administration, and judicial and administrative personnel.

Referring to a previous collegium resolution reiterating the recommendation of senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal for appointment as a judge, Justice Bhuyan said he found the reasons recorded by the Supreme Court convincing but noted that despite more than three and a half years having passed, no appointment materialised.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Key findings of the JALDI report reveal that only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for FY 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation.

Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets even as only two high courts publish disciplinary sanction orders pertaining to district judicial officers.

âThe findings highlight that the level of judicial transparency varies across courts and demonstrate that while individual disclosure measures have emerged...they have not yet translated into a holistic approach...â a release from Vidhi said.

World.title: July GST collections up 15.4% to Rs 2.1 L cr on higher imports
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: GST collections rose 15.4% to Rs 2,11,205 crore in July, the second highest since the new structure was implemented last Sept, on the back of a 29% jump in integrated GST (IGST) on imports. This was also the highest pace of growth since rate rationalisation.The rise in IGST on imports in July (for transactions in the previous month) may be attributed to higher prices of crude and other commodities in the wake of the West Asia conflict.The impact of strong economic activity in June, when factory output grew at its fastest pace in nearly two years, was also visible on the tax numbers, seen as an advance indicator of economic activity. Some of the price hikes in FMCG and automobile sectors would have also buoyed collections. Central GST mop-up was pegged 12.3% higher at just under Rs 40,000 crore, while state GST grew 8.7% to nearly Rs 48,000 crore."The high GST collections tie in very well with the 7.3% increase in industrial production during June. It reflects continued economic resilience despite the challenges in the external environment...Thesteady growth in GST collections each month indicates that overall domestic consumption is becoming largely insulated from seasonal variations and external headwinds," said MS Mani, partner at Deloitte India.Some experts, however, are worried about the continued rise in imports. "...one cannot ignore the elevated levels of import GST collections, which remain a nagging concern. This points to a persistent gap in domestic manufacturing capability despite the range of successful PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat interventions rolled out over the past few years.It is likely that the sustained push by policymakers towards localisation of around 100 products (being talked about) over a period of time will help bridge this gap," said Saurabh Agarwal, partner at EY India, a consulting firm.Net of refunds, which were 13% higher at almost Rs 30,000 crore, collections went up 15.8% to Rs 1,81,237 crore.Haryana logged the highest growth of 28%, followed by Gujarat and Puducherry (26%), Karnataka and Goa (23%), and Maharashtra (20%). Chhattisgarh (23% fall), Jharkhand and Manipur (20% decline) were among the laggards.

World.title: Government approves 2 tunnels for Valley-Jammu connectivity
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cabinet Friday approved two strategic tunnel projects and the approach roads on NH-244 in J&K at an estimated cost of around Rs 9,800 crore to provide all-weather connectivity between Kashmir Valley and Jammu region while improving access to Chenab Valley,.

The projects comprise Singhpora-Vailoo tunnel and Sudhmahadev-Dranga tunnel, along with their approach roads, on the Anantnag-Chenani corridor. These are expected to strengthen road connectivity in Doda, Kishtwar and Udhampur districts, and reduce travel time.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

While the development of the 39km Singhapora-Vailoo stretch will have 10km unidirectional twin-tube tunnels, the 13km Sudhmahadev-Dranga section will have 8km tunnels.

The projects would be completed in five years and will be fully Centre-funded.

The tunnels are aimed at bypassing difficult stretches of NH-244 that are frequently affected by adverse weather disrupting traffic and isolating several areas during the winter months. Once completed, the projects will provide a safer and more efficient route for commuters, tourists and freight movement. Officials said the projects would boost regional connectivity by ensuring year-round access to remote districts.

World.title: India-China border trade resumes after 6 years
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SHIMLA/PITHIRAGARH: India and China resumed traditional border trade Saturday through Lipulekh in Uttarakhand and Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh after nearly six years, restoring two key Himalayan trade routes that had remained closed since the Covid-19 pandemic.At Lipulekh in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh district, the first batch of 16 traders and four support staff crossed into Tibet without goods as the two sides began restoring trade operations. Chinese authorities restricted the inaugural batch to 20 people, citing infrastructure constraints at the Taklakot trade mart and sought detailed personal information of all traders in advance. They also asked that priority be given to those who had participated in the last trading season in 2019.Accordingly, the traders' association selected traders whose goods had remained stranded at Taklakot after trade was suspended in 2020. "Priority was given to traders who had participated in the 2019 trading season and had left their goods at Taklakot," Dharchula SDM and district trade officer Ashish Joshi said.Meanwhile, in Himachal Pradesh, revenue minister Jagat Singh Negi flagged off the first batch of 16 Indian traders as they set off with their horses towards Shipki village in Tibet through the 3,930-metre-high Shipki La Pass.The trade, suspended since 2020 because of Covid, was scheduled to resume on June 1 but was delayed owing to security concerns and inadequate infrastructure at the trading post.Trade through Shipki La, which will remain open until Nov 30, will continue under the traditional barter system. Indian traders will be allowed to stay across the border for up to 72 hours, while the home department has cleared 53 traders after verification of their antecedents.Indian traders have been permitted to export 36 categories of goods, including dried fruits, spices, handicrafts and herbs, while Chinese traders can bring 20 categories of goods, including pashmina, wool, yak hair, sheepskin, goatskin and China clay. Officials said the overall list comprised 72 categories of tradable goods from the Indian side and 30 from the Chinese side.Negi also inaugurated the Rs 1.7 crore Chhuppan Trade Mart at Namgya village in Pooh subdivision near the international border to facilitate border trade.Replying to a demand by local traders to expand the list of tradable goods, Negi said the proposal would be placed before CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and also with MEA.The routes were scheduled to reopen on June 1 but were delayed because of pending infrastructure and administrative preparations on both sides of the border. tnn(With inputs from Prem Punetha in Pithoragarh)

World.title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13 on Nazca Lines sightseeing flight
World.content:
A plane carrying tourists crashed into a field in Peru on Saturday (August 1, 2026) outside the city of Nazca killing 13 people, local authorities said.

In a statement on Facebook, Nazca’s municipal government said the plane was taking tourists on a sightseeing flight of the Nazca Lines, a group of extensive geoglyphs scraped into the desert around Nazca hundreds of years ago by Peru’s Indigenous inhabitants. The lines form images of animals that can only be fully appreciated from planes or viewing towers.

Nazca’s government said the plane departed from the nearby city of Ica and was operated by Peruvian company Aerodiana. On its website the airline says that it has offered scenic flights over the Nazca lines for the past 14 years, using Cessna Grand Caravan planes.

In a statement, Peru’s Ministry for Trade and Tourism said that 11 “foreign tourists” and two crew members were on the plane that crashed Saturday. State news agency Agencia Andina reported that two German, two Spanish and seven Italian tourists were on the plane.

Peruvian authorities said the accident is under investigation. Aerodiana was not immediately available for comment.

World.title: Bhogapuram airport built six months ahead of schedule: GMR Group Chairman
World.content:
GMR Group Chairman Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao looked jubilant and emotional during the inauguration of the international airport of Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district on Saturday. Hailing from Rajam in Vizianagaram district, Mr. Rao has a lot of experience in the aviation sector.

The GMR group has constructed the new airport at Bhogapuram, the native district of Mr. Rao. The GMR group has constructed the airport six months in advance of the deadline of December, he said.

“The Bhogapuram airport will help spur economic activity in the region, like the Shamshabad airport in Hyderabad. I am very happy that the airport has been built in my native district,” he said and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for extending support for the quick construction of the airport.

Currently, the GMR group handles airports in New Delhi, Hyderabad and other places in the country.

World.title: Narendra Modi all praise for Bobbili Veena artisans
World.content:
Bobbili Veena, a famous traditional string instrument from Andhra Pradesh, hogged the limelight again at the inauguration of the Bhogapuram aiport on Saturday. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu presented a Bobbili Veena to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Thanking Mr. Naidu fior the gesture, the Prime Minister made a post on social media platform X. “Bobbili Veena has a special place in India’s musical traditions. (I am) delighted to receive the exquisitely handcrafted Bobbili Ekanda Veena in Bhogapuram. It embodies the skills of AP’s artisans. My compliments to them for preserving the culture of the State,” Mr. Modi posted.

Bobbili Veena is crafted in the heritage city of Bobbili in Vizianagaram district. The instrument has gained nationwide prominence due to patronage from great musicians across the country.

World.title: Bhogapuram airport a historic chapter for Uttarandhra, says Union Civil Aviation Minister
World.content:
Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu on Saturday hailed the inauguration of the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram as a historic milestone that would transform the future of Uttarandhra and remain etched in people’s memories for generations.

The Union Minister described the event as far more than a government programme, calling it a celebration for every household in Andhra Pradesh.

Addressing the inaugural ceremony in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and other dignitaries, Mr. Rammohan Naidu said that after assuming office as the Union Civil Aviation Minister, he had the privilege of inaugurating 16 aviation-related projects with the Prime Minister.

Noting that none of those projects had witnessed such huge public participation, he said that the occasion held a special significance for himself as a native of Uttarandhra.

Mr. Rammohan Naidu recalled that Mr. Chandrababu Naidu had initiated the Bhogapuram airport project during his earlier tenure, while then Union Civil Aviation Minister P. Ashok Gajapathi Raju had played a key role in taking it forward and Prime Minister Narendra Modi finally made it happen.

It is a remarkable coincidence that the airport was finally inaugurated during the NDA’s tenure, with himself serving as the Union Civil Aviation Minister.

The Union Minister expressed confidence that the new international airport would open up unprecedented opportunities in investment, tourism, trade, industry and employment, while placing the region prominently on the global map. He said that the Centre was planning to establish training facilities for the aviation workforce in the region to equip the local youth with skills and generate employment opportunities in the fast-growing aviation sector.

Bhogapuram airport would also boost tourism and improve connectivity to the region’s prominent religious destinations. Besides, the present projects such as Google data centre, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel (AM/NS) project and the South Coast Railway Zone, together would make Uttarandhra a major economic hub, he added.

World.title: Vizianagaram district administration gets a pat
World.content:
The Vizianagaram district administration was appreciated by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for hosting the inauguration of the Bhogapuram airport within less than a month. The inauguration was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Chief Minister and a host of dignitaries.

Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy got appreciation for successful conduct of the programme. Mr. Ramsundar Reddy told the media that event was organised with the coordination with all the stakeholders, public and media.

World.title: Pawan Kalyan gets a special handshake from PM Modi
World.content:
Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan got a special handshake from Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the inauguration of the Bhogapuram airport on Saturday. After speeches, Mr. Modi briefly interacted with Mr. Pawan and enquired about his health as the latter underwent surgery on his shoulder recently.

Wearing a sling, Mr. Pawan Kalyan attended the first public meeting and shared the dais with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

World.title: 3 people killed, at least 21 wounded in Moscow restaurant bombing, Russian officials say
World.content:
A bomb detonated at ​a ​restaurant on Saturday (August 1, 2026) in ‌central ⁠Moscow killing at least three people, including the bomber, Russian state media ​said, ​citing ​local officials.

At least 21 people were also injured when the explosive device detonated at the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in Moscow, the National Anti-Terrorism Committee said, quoted by Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.

An unidentified woman who attempted to carry the explosive device into the restaurant died in the blast as did a security guard and a patron, the news agency said.

Ria Novosti reported the woman attempted to smuggle the bomb into the establishment but the security guard refused to let her in before the bomb exploded.

The attack was still being investigated, the Moscow Investigative Committee told the news agency.

World.title: Digital medical emergency referral system set to transform patient care in Rajasthan
World.content:
A new digital medical emergency referral system being rolled out in Rajasthan is set to transform patient care during the critical initial hours. The model will enable the tertiary hospitals to make preparations for attending to the patients even before they arrive.

Rajasthan is the first State in the country to implement the model, in which a referred patient’s medical history will reach the control room online before they arrive at the hospital. This will allow a team of medical experts to review the reports and stand ready for treatment.

Prepared and tested at Rabindranath Tagore Medical College in Udaipur, the Sim­pli­fied Emergency Trans­fer and Urgent Refer­ral (SETU) has already man­aged over 3,510 emer­gency cases across 15 dis­tricts in the State. The model is going to be a lifesaver for patients by eliminating the issue of “blind arrivals”.

Principal Medical and Health Secretary Gayatri Rathore said in Jaipur on Saturday (august 1, 2026) that the SETU would serve as a robust digital bridge connecting the primary health centres (PHC) and community health centres (CHC) in the remote rural areas with medical colleges and tertiary hospitals in the cities.

“The system operates using only smartphones, quick response (QR) codes, and a closed user group (CUG) network, eliminating the need for heavy investments in additional infrastructure,” Ms. Rathore said. As soon as a physician at a PHC refers a patient using the digital app, the complete digital data, estimated time of arrival and live GPS tracking will be sent to the tertiary hospital.

Before the patient reaches the hospital, the control room will alert super-specialists in the relevant departments, such as trauma, surgical, obstetrics and gynaecology, and paediatrics, via the CUG network and reserve intensive care unit or emergency beds.

Ms. Rathore said a fully prepared team of doctors would begin the life-saving treatment for the patient from “minute zero”, as soon as the ambulance doors open. Besides, every patient referred through SETU will receive a fol­low-up call from the con­trol room on the fol­low­ing day to obtain feed­back on treat­ment and hos­pital ser­vices.

World.title: Second phase of AJK elections on Sunday in 9 Muzaffarabad division, 12 refugee constituencies
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Polling for the second phase of elections to the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly will be held on Sunday in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 constituencies reserved for Kashmiri refugees settled in Pakistan, where more than 340 candidates are contesting 21 seats.

According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts.

Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu.

A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, including 427,955 men and 381,666 women.

The 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834, comprising 247,776 male and 191,054 female voters.

Internet services were suspended again on Friday, less than 45 hours after being restored, as part of efforts to discourage elements attempting to disrupt the election process. Official sources said the services were likely to be restored on Sunday.

However, the Election Commission made it clear that polling would be held as scheduled in all nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and the 12 refugee constituencies.

It added that polling would continue from 8am to 5pm without a break.

Election material had been delivered to all polling stations in the 12 refugee constituencies, the commission said, adding that the distribution of polling material had also been completed in all constituencies of Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts, while the process had entered its final stage in the five constituencies of Muzaffarabad district.

Polling staff had also been dispatched to their respective polling stations under stringent security arrangements.

According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal.

Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies.

It said all administrative and security arrangements had been completed and security personnel had already been deployed at polling stations to ensure the peaceful conduct of polling.

Separately, in a televised message to the public on the eve of polling, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal urged voters to exercise their right to franchise, saying the vote was the only means through which citizens could choose a better future and capable leadership.

“There is no substitute for the vote, and every citizen should fulfil this national responsibility,” he said, adding that the vote was a trust that should be entrusted to an honest and competent candidate.

Mughal appealed to the electorate to participate wholeheartedly in the democratic process and demonstrate responsible citizenship. He said all arrangements had been finalised to ensure peaceful, transparent and fair elections.

During the first phase of elections in Mirpur division, the PML-N grabbed nine out of the 13 constituencies.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on June 27. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice.

According to preliminary results issued by the AJK Election Commission (Forms-27), the PML-N emerged as the winner in nine constituencies, while the PPP could secure only four seats.

World.title: Army major martyred in North Waziristan IBO: ISPR
World.content:
An army officer was martyred during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Razmak area of North Waziristan district, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement on Saturday.

During the operation, security forces also killed five terrorists affiliated with Fitna al Khawarij, according to the military’s media wing.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

The ISPR said that Major Hafiz Ihsan Elahi, 34, from Mianwali district, was “a brave officer who was leading his troops from the front, fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifice” and embraced martyrdom.

Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed terrorists, “who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities” against security forces and law enforcement agencies, as well as in the killing of civilians.

“Sanitisation operations are being conducted to eliminate any other India-sponsored terrorist found in the area. Relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” the ISPR statement read.

“Such sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment of safeguarding our nation at all costs.”

Earlier this week, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the government was implementing a comprehensive and effective strategy to “completely eliminate” the menace posed by the proscribed Fitna-al-Hindustan, Fitna-al-Khawarij and other terrorist outfits to the country.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism since the banned TTP ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks.

Last month, in the wake of multiple major attacks in Balochistan, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir had reaffirmed that terrorism “emanating from across the borders will be crushed with full might of the state”.

On July 29, the military’s media wing said security forces killed 32 terrorists during operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

7 terrorists killed in Nushki IBO

In a separate statement, ISPR said security forces killed “seven Indian-sponsored terrorists” during an IBO in Balochistan’s Nushki district on the night of July 30/31 July.

Among those was a would-be suicide bomber, the ISPR said, noting that the IBO was carried out on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan” — a term designated by the state for terrorist organisations in Balo­chistan.

During the operation, a terrorist hideout was “identified, monitored and busted through prompt surgical action by own forces, killing all seven Indian sponsored terrorists, including a suicide bomber”, the statement said.

It added that ammunition and improvised explosive devices found there were also destroyed on-site.

Sanitisation operations were underway to eliminate “any other Indian sponsored terrorist found in the area”.

The military’s media affairs wing reaffirmed that the counter-terrorism campaign under Vision Azm-i-Istehkam would continue “at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and -supported terrorism from the country”.

A day earlier, Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti vowed that the state would not retreat “even an inch” in its fight against terrorism.

Last month, security forces killed at least 16 terrorists during “Operation Al-Azm” in Balochistan’s Mastung district, which was launched after a shooting on a Karachi-bound coach claimed three lives and injured five others.

Security concerns heightened in Balochistan after a spate of major terrorist attacks took place in early July, which prompted counterterrorism operations across the province.

World.title: Bilawal receives JAAC response on reconciliation commission, says AJK PM to consult stakeholders on way forward
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Saturday said he had received a response from the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) to his letter proposing the establishment of a Truth and Reconciliation Commission, adding that the party would now consult key stakeholders to determine the way forward.

The PPP has repeatedly called for the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission amid protests in AJK.

Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues — most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly reserved for refugees from Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir who settled in mainland Pakistan after 1947, which has resulted in protests across the region.

In a post on X, Bilawal welcomed the group’s “willingness to engage with the proposed commission” as a possible institutional mechanism to address the crisis, noting that the proposal had also been endorsed by the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly.

The PPP chairman maintained that his “foremost priority” is to help bring an end to the “ongoing crisis” and provide relief to the region’s people and restore normal life in AJK as “soon as possible”.

“The loss of every precious life is a national tragedy.”

Bilawal said he would now consult AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who would seek initial input from the federal government and other relevant stakeholders to determine whether there was sufficient common ground to move forward with a mutually agreed proposal.

Earlier, Bilawal said he had been campaigning for the formation of the commission for the past month.

Addressing a public gathering of party workers in Muzaffarabad earlier this week, the PPP chairman said: “It is necessary that during these historic elections, we restore peace and maintain fairness and transparency. To honour the future of Kashmir and Pakistan’s stance on Kashmir, this is not about anyone’s victory or defeat. The state and the protesters will have to accept this recommendation from the PPP.”

The region’s legislative assembly had also endorsed a resolution asking for the establishment of an independent reconciliation commission to investigate the violence and pave the way for a negotiated settlement.

JAAC ban

The regional government on June 5 declared the JAAC a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act.

The notification by AJK’s Home Department said the group was “engaged in terrorism” and acted in a manner “prejudicial to peace and security” of the state.

It further stated that JAAC was involved in “creating anarchy in the state by intimidating public, promoting hatred and creating a sense of insecurity in society and public at large etc”.

Following the ban, local authorities launched a crackdown against the organisation, arresting scores of its leaders and activists from different areas.

In a televised press conference on July 28, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar alleged the involvement of militant elements within JAAC, adding that they were pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding.

The information minister reiterated claims made earlier in the day by the region’s information secretary and a senior police official that a significant number of protesters participating in the proscribed JAAC demonstration in AJK were affiliated with Fitna Al Khawarij.

World.title: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, others perish in Broad Peak avalanche, climbing company confirms
World.content:
Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja died along with other team members in a powerful avalanche on Broad Peak, his climbing company confirmed on Saturday.

The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by 43-year-old British-Nepali climber Purja.

“It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak,” Purja’s company Elite Expeditions said on social media.

“We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive,” it added.

The remains recovered so far — flown by helicopter to hospital for formal identification — included an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man, the Gilgit-Baltistan government said in a statement released on Friday night.

Purja, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, broke multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah offered his condolences over the “tragic” deaths of Purja and the other climbers, which he said “has shocked us”.

“The physical journey of all the deceased climbers… has been interrupted, but the history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring,” Shah said in a statement on social media.

Police in GB said in a statement that high-altitude porters and rescue teams were carrying out a second day of the operation on Saturday after the search was paused due to difficult weather conditions a day earlier.

Rescuers and army helicopters had been scouring the area and teams stayed at the base camp overnight, according to the GB government.

“The rescue operation is being conducted under extremely challenging terrain and high-altitude weather conditions by the Pakistani army in coordination with local high-altitude climbers and rescuers,” it said.

Powerful avalanche

The avalanche struck while the mountaineers were on a mission to summit Broad Peak (8,047 metres, or 26,400 feet) on Thursday and while the team was ascending at an altitude of around 6,600 metres, according to regional authorities.

The expedition comprised 10 people — including Purja, five Nepalis, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, and a climber from China.

The team was last in contact on Thursday morning, the official statement said, with reports emerging that evening of the powerful avalanche.

“Data from their tracking devices indicates that they were thrown hundreds of metres down the mountainside,” Naila Kiani, from Pakistan’s Alpine Club, told Le Monde newspaper.

Fida Ali, a climber in the area who worked closely with Purja since 2023, told AFP their focus for the climbing season was summiting Broad Peak, but they had first tackled another mountain, G2, in harsh weather.

Ali also joined the expedition to Broad Peak in its initial stages but returned early to accompany a Russian climber who was feeling the effects of exhaustion — narrowly avoiding the fatal avalanche.

“I wanted to go with him (Purja) but couldn’t and came back with her. I was part of the team but survived,” he told AFP.

Super peaks

Purja had written on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 “super peaks” twice without oxygen.

“Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down,” he wrote.

He had climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders” (peaks above 8,000 metres) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 — then a record.

Broad Peak is the world’s 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents.

It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.

World.title: US to make visa bond programme permanent for people from dozens of countries
World.content:
The US State Department will make permanent a visa bond programme that could require applicants from 50 countries, mostly from Africa, to post bonds of up to $20,000 when seeking US visas, according to a federal notice posted online on Friday.

The Federal Register notice applies to B1 and B2 visas, which are issued for business and tourism travel.

“Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers,” the notice said.

“The 2025 visa bond pilot, which provided a framework for the Department of State, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Department of the Treasury to assess the feasibility of administering a visa bond programme, has provided sufficient data to suggest that a visa bond programme is an effective tool for enforcing compliance among bonded visa holders.”

In the pilot programme, consular officers could require bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or up to $15,000. The final rule eliminates the $5,000 option and raises the maximum bond to $20,000.

The final rule goes into effect on August 3 when it is scheduled for publication in the Federal Register. In the list of 50 countries for whose citizens this programme applies, 30 are from Africa.

US officials say the policy is intended to reduce visa overstays. Immigration advocates argue it will deter legitimate travel to the United States.

Rights advocates say President Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown violates free speech and due process, while creating an unsafe environment for ethnic minorities and encouraging racial profiling. Trump has defended the measures as necessary to bolster national security.

While Trump says he wants to curb illegal immigration, his administration has made legal immigration more difficult, for example, by imposing new and expensive fees for applicants of certain visas and by enforcing social media vetting for applicants and immigrants already in the country.

Earlier in May, the State Department identified nationals from the following 50 countries as being required to post visa bonds: Algeria, Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Bangladesh, Benin, Bhutan, Botswana, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Central African Republic, Cote D’Ivoire, Cuba, Djibouti, Dominica, Ethiopia, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Georgia, Grenada, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kyrgyz Republic, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mongolia, Mozambique, Namibia, Nepal, Nicaragua, Nigeria, Papua New Guinea, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu, Venezuela, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

World.title: PML-N, PPP leaders resume talks to ease tensions over AJK polls
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Senior leaders of the PML-N and PPP on Saturday resumed talks aimed at defusing tensions between the two parties following the latter’s allegations of rigging in four of the 13 constituencies in Mirpur division during the first phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections.

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling.

The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings — the first at a local hotel on Thursday night and the second before noon on Friday.

The PML-N delegation comprised Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah, Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, and PML-N AJK chapter secretary general and MLA-elect Chaudhry Tariq Farooq.

Representing the PPP were former Senate chairman Nayyar Bokhari, former federal minister Qamar Zaman Kaira and AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who also serves as secretary general of the party’s AJK chapter.

PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan attended the Friday meeting but was absent from today’s session.

The meetings reviewed security arrangements ahead of the second phase of polling on Sunday. Both sides agreed that the Election Commission, as well as the divisional and district administrations, should leave no room for lapses in ensuring extraordinary security measures so that voters could exercise their franchise freely.

According to sources, the discussions also focused on the PPP’s allegations of rigging and its subsequent demand for repolling in certain constituencies.

The PPP was told that neither the government nor any institution had facilitated or backed rigging and that, if irregularities had occurred at any polling station, they were localised incidents rather than the result of any organised plan.

“It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” a source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts.

The PML-N leadership maintained that, unlike the PPP, it had begun election preparations well in advance and had enforced greater organisational discipline through constituency-level planning.

The PPP, they claimed, had remained under the impression that the elections would be delayed by a year and that the 12 refugee constituencies would be abolished, which prevented it from focusing on electoral preparations in time.

The meeting also discussed ways to address the complaints through both political dialogue and legal channels, the source said.

According to the sources, the PPP had initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies: Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala.

Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK president Chaudhry Yasin lost to the PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by the PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed.

The sources said the PML-N had presented a detailed analysis of the results, showing that while its candidates had secured more than 80 per cent of the votes at some polling stations, the PPP had also won more than 80pc of the votes at others.

“If any irregularities occurred, they occurred on both sides, and a mechanism has been discussed to address them, legally and politically,” said a PML-N leader.

The meeting tasked both regional secretary generals — Rathore and Farooq — with contacting the Election Commission to explore a legal resolution to the dispute.

Another meeting had been scheduled for Saturday afternoon, but it could not be held because Sanaullah and Muqam had to leave for Islamabad owing to urgent engagements.

Both parties traded barbs earlier this week after the conclusion of the first phase of elections in AJK, with the PPP chairman alleging rigging in the polls and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz urging the PPP to accept defeat.

The PML-N grabbed nine out of the 13 constituencies of AJK’s Mirpur division in the elections.

In a televised statement, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz hailed the “outstanding victory” of the PML-N in the first phase of the AJK elections, urging the PPP to accept defeat.

“The PPP should have accepted its defeat by affirming the spirit of democracy, but I felt aggrieved by the kind of words used by PPP leaders.”

“The state does not decide election results; only the people make this decision,” she said in response to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations.

On Thursday, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned that a stolen election in AJK would start a “countdown” for the federal government.

“If you steal [the election] … write it down, take my guarantee, that a countdown will start for your federal government,” he warned. “If you steal my mandate, I will come for your throne.”

World.title: PPP, PML-N continue war of words on eve of Muzaffarabad elections
World.content:
The PPP and the PML-N continued lambasting each other on Saturday, extending their rhetoric from the ongoing elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) to the other party’s previous tenures in power.

The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged as the winner in the elections in AJK’s Mirpur division. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling.

Political temperatures remain high as the second phase of AJK elections is set to be held tomorrow in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division. The third phase is scheduled for August 10 in all 12 refugee constituencies and 11 constituencies of Poonch division.

In the latest exchange, PML-N senior leader Rana Sanaullah remarked on President Asif Ali Zardari’s role as he responded to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections.

“If you call the votes secured by the prime minister votes of Forms-47, then on what forms has the president gotten votes on?” Sanaullah said.

On Wednesday, Bilawal had taken a direct jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, saying: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.”

Sanaullah, also the prime minister’s aide on political affairs and a federal minister, was addressing a gathering in Jhelum Valley alongside Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam.

Sanaullah further said: “If you say to Mian Nawaz Sharif that he became the prime minister for the first time or every time through rigging, […] then remember, it is also discussed here that someone also became the prime minister for the first time after breaking apart the country.”

He was referring to PPP founder Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became the president of Pakistan in December 1971 after the secession of Bangladesh (then-East Pakistan) following the 1970 elections.

In August 1973, Bhutto took the oath as the prime minister in 1973 under the new Constitution.

Sanaullah also took a jibe at Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, whose recent remarks have sparked a fresh debate in political circles on the matter of creating new provinces.

Calling Naqvi a “blessed one” of President Zardari, the PML-N leader said the interior minister had “made the [political] journey of 30 years in three-and-a-half years”.

“You began from where and have now reached where, and now you realise that this system is completely dysfunctional.”

In his speech, Muqam criticised the PPP’s governance in Sindh, saying that no performance of the party could be seen.

He also said the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) — a scheme that the PPP often takes credit for launching — was not “anyone’s personal programme but the government’s”.

Earlier on Saturday, PPP leader Saeed Ghani alleged that the PML-N had never won a general election without rigging.

This followed a press briefing by Punjab’s education and sports ministers, where they said that the chief ministers of Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had nothing to show for their performance.

PML-N never won an election without rigging: Ghani

Addressing a press conference in Karachi, Ghani said, “The PPP did not secure power through rigging in any of the elections held till today.

“On the other hand, however many times the PML-N has secured power, it has not been without rigging.”

PPP leader Saeed Ghani addresses a press conference in Karachi on Aug 1, 2026. — DawnNewsTV

Ghani, also the Sindh labour minister, made the allegation as he responded to a PML-N member calling on the PPP to not “give lectures on democracy”.

“If you do not want to give the PPP the right to speak on democracy, then will you give it to Gen Musharraf or Gen Zia, or the leaders created by them?” he quipped, referring to the two former military dictators.

The PPP leader said he “did count the 1985 election”, alleging that PML-N supremo and ex-premier Nawaz Sharif “conspired” against ex-prime minister Mohammad Khan Junejo.

He further claimed that his party “became a target of rigging” in the 1988 and 1990 elections, which resulted in the PML-N winning. He went on to allege that the PPP was again “controlled and prevented from forming a government in Punjab” in 1993.

Ghani alleged that the PPP was restricted to “16-17 seats” in the 1997 general elections, when Nawaz’s PML-N again formed the government.

He contended that although the PPP secured power in 2008, the “PML-N was made to win seats, especially in Punjab, through rigging during Musharraf’s tenure”.

Ghani claimed that the PML-N was “made to win” the 2013 elections as well.

“Then the elections in 2024 [took place]. No matter how many times they say, everyone, even children, know that the PML-N was badly defeated in the elections,” he asserted.

The PPP leader alleged that Nawaz, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz “lost their own seats and then blame us”.

Ghani made the remarks after explaining the rationale for his party’s stances on new provinces in Sindh and Punjab, stressing that it was based on the wishes of the people.

He emphasised that the Constitution required any such move to be made through the elected representatives in the provincial assembly concerned.

He noted that the “people of Sindh, its representatives and its assembly say there is no need for further provinces in Sindh”.

On the other hand, Ghani pointed out, the Punjab Assembly and the Senate had passed resolutions over a decade ago calling for two new provinces in Punjab.

“If the people and the elected representatives of Sindh say that there is no need for any new province in Sindh, then no one in Punjab has the right to say whether there should be a new province in Sindh or not,” Ghani asserted.

He went on to stress that the PPP advocated for more provinces in Punjab as the “people of Punjab and their elected representatives” desired that.

The PPP leader emphasised that his party “represented” the citizens of each of the provinces when taking a stance for Sindh and Punjab.

At the outset of his press conference, Ghani also took exception to comments made by “two ministers”, saying it seemed that they “did not know anything about Sindh”.

“They are restricted within a circle called Maryam Nawaz. They only see and say what she tells them, shows them and explains to them,” he said in an apparent reference to the Punjab ministers.

World.title: ‘Enough is enough’: MQM-P leaders, Shahid Khaqan back creation of new administrative units
World.content:
Former premier Shahid Khaqan Abbasi and MQM-P leaders Dr Farooq Sattar and Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Saturday backed the creation of additional administrative units in the country.

On Thursday, Naqvi urged all political parties to “settle” various national-level issues, including the question of creating new provinces .

Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 being held in Islamabad, Naqvi said there was “only one solution” to improving the country’s overall condition: “You will have to take [the matter of] administrative units, provinces or whatever you may call it, to the public.”

Addressing a press conference in Karachi today, MQM leader Dr Farooq Sattar said that, due to immense population growth, additional administrative units were essential to ensure proper governance.

“No country in the world has seen population growth as fast as ours,” he said. “We need to manage and administer that, but how will we do that without additional administrative units?”

Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui and MQM Deputy Convener Dr Farooq Sattar address a press conference in Karachi on August 1, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/Dawn News

Sattar noted that, with such a large population, questions arose about how administrations would be able to address fundamental issues and ensure effective service delivery.

“Two things have become clear: we need administrative units. Enough is enough,” he declared.

“The ad-hocism we have seen for around 80 years must end. [Interior Minister] Mohsin Naqvi presented a clear administrative framework for Pakistan’s future in his speech, which is welcomed by citizens from all walks of life.”

“Pakistan’s economy is tied to its political and administrative structure.”

“We need curative treatment, not symptomatic treatment,” he stated.

Sattar added that the door needs to be left open for Gen-Z to play a representative role in Pakistan’s political, economic and social landscape.
